arxiv-2402-18104.description: Abstract In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated notable success across various tasks, but the trustworthiness of LLMs is still an open problem. One specific threat is the potential to generate toxic or harmful responses. Attackers can craft adversarial prompts that induce harmful responses from LLMs.

arxiv-2410-01697.title: Enhancing Adversarial Robustness through Multi-Objective Representation Learning
arxiv-2410-01697.creator: Sedjro Salomon Hotegni(✉), Sebastian Peitz
arxiv-2410-01697.description: Abstract Deep neural networks (DNNs) are vulnerable to small adversarial perturbations, which are tiny changes to the input data that appear insignificant but cause the model to produce drastically different outputs. Many defense methods require modifying model architectures during evaluation or performing test-time data purification. This not only introduces additional complexity but is often architecture-dependent.

pmc-10656465.title: Unveiling the influence of task-relevance of emotional faces on behavioral reactions in a multi-face context using a novel Flanker-Go/No-go task
pmc-10656465.creator: Martina Montalti, Giovanni Mirabella
pmc-10656465.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Recent research indicates that emotional faces affect motor control only when task-relevant. However, these studies utilized a single-face presentation, which does not accurately mirror real-life situations wherein we frequently engage with multiple individuals simultaneously. To overcome this limitation, we gave 40 participants two versions of a novel Flanker-Go/No-go task, where we presented three-face stimuli with a central target and two task-irrelevant flankers that could be congruent or incongruent with the target for valence and gender.

pmc-12583239.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Extreme weather events (EWEs) continue to threaten the health and well‐being of populations across the globe. However, risk from drought and floods is not evenly distributed spatially nor are all populations equally at risk for poor health outcomes. Globally, people living with HIV/AIDS (PLHIV) face a particular set of challenges with EWE exposure including increased susceptibility to disease progression from care disruptions and medication adherence, and general population concentration in areas where rainfall is both highly variable and key to economic well‐being.

pmc-13541768.creator: Qi Tang, Liyuan Hu, Minxiang Xie, Ran Zhan, Qiao Wang, Rong Zhang
